annotation_description: In competitive Modern, choosing to be on the play is almost always correct. Being on the play gives you tempo advantage - you get to deploy threats and disruption (like Thoughtseize) a turn earlier. The extra card from being on the draw is rarely worth the tempo loss, especially with a hand containing Thoughtseize which is significantly better on turn 1 on the play (before the opponent has had a chance to deploy anything). This deck with Orcish Bowmasters, Thoughtseize, and Phelia is a tempo-oriented deck that benefits greatly from being on the play.

Playing the singleton Scalding Tarn instead of one of the two Bloodstained Mires. Since the player already has an Island in hand, Scalding Tarn's unique utility (fetching Islands) is less immediately needed. Saving Scalding Tarn for later preserves more flexibility, as having both Scalding Tarn and Bloodstained Mire available later covers more options (Island/Mountain + Swamp/Mountain) than two Bloodstained Mires (Swamp/Mountain only).

Fetched Steam Vents (paying 2 life to enter untapped) when a basic Mountain would have provided the needed {R} for Dragon's Rage Channeler while saving 2 life. With Island already in hand and two Bloodstained Mires for future color fixing, the dual land's flexibility is less necessary. In Modern, where life is a critical resource (especially with Mutagenic Growth in hand costing 2 life via Phyrexian mana), saving 2 life could matter.

Casting Dragon's Rage Channeler before Mishra's Bauble is a sequencing error. Mishra's Bauble is a noncreature spell that costs 0 mana, so casting it first (or after DRC) would trigger DRC's surveil ability. However, the optimal play is to cast DRC first, then cast Mishra's Bauble to trigger the surveil. Wait - actually, let me reconsider. If you cast DRC first, then Bauble, you get a surveil trigger from Bauble. If you cast Bauble first, then DRC, you get no surveil trigger but Bauble is already in the graveyard as an artifact type. Actually, casting DRC first then Bauble is correct - you get the surveil trigger AND the artifact goes to the graveyard. So DRC first is actually the right sequencing here.

Dragon's Rage Channeler is a 1/1 facing an empty board. Skipping the attack phase leaves 1 free damage on the table. While not casting Mutagenic Growth precombat is defensible (saving the card), there's no reason not to attack with an unblocked creature.

Gem3F Vorthos has Lava Dart in the graveyard, which can be flashed back by sacrificing a Mountain (Steam Vents counts as a Mountain). At the end of the opponent's turn, this is generally free mana-wise since it's the opponent's end step and the Steam Vents is already tapped. Flashing back Lava Dart would deal 1 damage to the opponent (or save it for a creature), trigger Dragon's Rage Channeler's surveil ability (it's a noncreature spell), and add an exile-zone card type or at minimum help fuel delirium. Currently the graveyard has Land (Scalding Tarn), Instant (Lava Dart), and Artifact (Mishra's Bauble) — three types. The DRC needs 4 types for delirium. Casting Lava Dart from the graveyard would trigger surveil, potentially putting a 4th card type into the graveyard to enable delirium. Additionally, the Lava Dart would go to exile after flashback, so it wouldn't add a type, but the surveil trigger could put a sorcery or creature into the graveyard. Sacrificing Steam Vents is a real cost, but with two Bloodstained Mires and an Island in hand, the mana base can recover. This is at least worth considering, though sacrificing the only land in play on turn 1 is aggressive. The surveil to enable delirium on DRC (making it a 3/3 flyer) could be very significant.

Declining to cast Mutagenic Growth on an unblocked Dragon's Rage Channeler. While saving the trick for later has merit, casting it here would provide a free surveil trigger (helping dig toward delirium for DRC) and deal 2 extra damage at the cost of 2 life. The surveil is particularly valuable since DRC needs a 4th card type in the graveyard for delirium, which would make it a 3/3 flyer.

Playing Bloodstained Mire as the land drop instead of Island. The basic Island provides the same mana without costing life, while preserving both Bloodstained Mires for future revolt triggers, instant-speed shuffle effects, and deck thinning at optimal moments.

Cracking Bloodstained Mire before casting Preordain is suboptimal sequencing. Casting Preordain first would let them scry 2 to arrange their library before the fetch shuffle, and would immediately trigger DRC's surveil and put a sorcery in the graveyard, achieving delirium (land + instant + artifact + sorcery = 4 types) before combat, making DRC a 3/3 flyer for the attack step.

Fetched Steam Vents (paying 2 life to enter untapped) when a basic Mountain would have served the same purpose. Already has Steam Vents on board for blue mana and Island in hand. The 2 life is wasted since red mana and Lava Dart flashback fuel are the main needs from this fetch.

Casting Preordain before playing a land is a sequencing error. Gem3F has Island and Bloodstained Mire in hand. They should play the land first (Island), then cast Preordain. Playing the land first preserves optionality - if Preordain reveals something that changes what land they want to play, they've already committed. More importantly, playing Island first and keeping Bloodstained Mire in hand preserves the fetch land for later turns where Revolt enablement (for Fatal Push from opponent) or shuffle effects matter. However, the DRC surveil trigger from Preordain could influence what they want to do with their land drop, so there's some argument for casting first. But generally, playing lands before spells is correct sequencing since it costs nothing and preserves information advantage.

Fetched Godless Shrine instead of basic Swamp against an aggressive deck (Dragon's Rage Channeler, Lava Dart in graveyard). The only spell they need to cast this turn is Thoughtseize (requiring {B}), and white mana isn't needed until next turn when Flooded Strand can fetch a white source. Paying 2 extra life to shock in Godless Shrine is unnecessary against a burn/prowess deck.

Playing Undercity Sewers (which enters tapped) instead of Flooded Strand means the player cannot cast Thoughtseize this turn, losing a critical turn of information and disruption against an aggressive opponent. Flooded Strand could fetch Godless Shrine or another untapped dual to have two mana available immediately. The opponent has Dragon's Rage Channeler attacking and is clearly on a fast aggro/tempo deck - delaying Thoughtseize by a turn is meaningful. Additionally, playing Flooded Strand first would enable revolt for Fatal Push if needed, allowing it to kill creatures with mana value 4 or less.

Casting Thoughtseize over Fatal Push is debatable here. The opponent has a Dragon's Rage Channeler on the battlefield (tapped, likely attacked last turn) with 6 cards in graveyard - close to achieving delirium (they have Instant, Artifact, Sorcery, Land, Creature types visible, so DRC likely already has delirium and is a 3/3). Fatal Push would cleanly remove DRC (mana value 1, well within range), and with Polluted Delta in graveyard, revolt could even be enabled later by cracking Flooded Strand. However, Thoughtseize has merit - seeing the opponent's hand and stripping a key card (like Expressive Iteration or Mutagenic Growth) could be more impactful, especially since Kimi25 has Phelia coming down next turn and wants to protect it. The opponent also has an untapped Steam Vents, meaning they could have Lightning Bolt or other interaction. Thoughtseize lets you see what's coming and potentially strip removal before deploying Phelia. Still, removing DRC immediately with Fatal Push while it's the only threat on board, and saving Thoughtseize for when you have more information or when sequencing matters more, seems like a reasonable alternative line. This is close enough that it's debatable rather than clearly wrong.

The opponent has a Dragon's Rage Channeler on board (already with delirium likely enabled given 4+ card types in graveyard: land, instant, sorcery, artifact) and Lightning Bolt in hand. Kimi25 Libby is at 14 life (about to go to 12 from Thoughtseize). Taking Lightning Bolt would remove 3 damage and protect Phelia (which they're about to deploy) from removal. Expressive Iteration is strong card advantage, but Lightning Bolt is both a direct threat to life total and can kill Phelia. With the opponent's aggressive burn strategy and DRC already threatening significant damage, taking the Lightning Bolt could be more immediately impactful. However, taking Expressive Iteration to deny card advantage is a defensible choice since it prevents the opponent from refueling.

There is a lethal line available: Crack Bloodstained Mire for Mountain, tap Mountain to cast Lightning Bolt at opponent (3 damage, Slickshot +2/+0), cast Mutagenic Growth paying 2 life (Slickshot +2/+0 and +2/+2), sacrifice Mountain for Lava Dart flashback at opponent (1 damage, Slickshot +2/+0). Slickshot attacks as 9/4 flying for 9 + 3 + 1 = 13 damage against opponent at 12 life. This is exact lethal that must not be missed.

message: Pick triggered ability (goes to the stack first)
annotation_description: Gem3F Vorthos missed lethal. With Mutagenic Growth on the stack, they could sacrifice Bloodstained Mire to fetch a Mountain, then flashback Lava Dart targeting the opponent for 1 damage. Lava Dart would trigger prowess on both Dragon's Rage Channeler and Slickshot Show-Off. Total damage: DRC (3/3 delirium + 1 Mutagenic prowess + 1 Lava Dart prowess = 5) + Slickshot (3/1 + 2/2 Mutagenic Growth + 1/1 Mutagenic prowess + 1/1 Lava Dart prowess = 7) + 1 Lava Dart direct = 13 damage against 12 life.

Gem3F Vorthos has the opponent at 4 life with Lava Dart available to flashback from the graveyard (by sacrificing a Mountain - but they don't have an untapped Mountain... wait, let me check). They have Bloodstained Mire untapped which could fetch a Mountain, but they also have Lightning Bolt in hand. Actually, looking more carefully: the opponent is at 4 life. Gem3F has Lightning Bolt in hand (3 damage) and Lava Dart in graveyard (1 damage flashback by sacrificing a Mountain). They could crack Bloodstained Mire to get a Mountain (going to 11 life), then cast Lightning Bolt (3 damage, opponent to 1), then flashback Lava Dart sacrificing the Mountain (1 damage, opponent to 0) for lethal. Both Steam Vents are tapped, but Bloodstained Mire is untapped - they can fetch an untapped Mountain, use it for Lightning Bolt, then sacrifice it for Lava Dart flashback. That's exactly 4 damage for lethal. They declined to activate Bloodstained Mire here, missing the kill.

Gem3F Vorthos has the opponent at 4 life with Lava Dart available to flashback from the graveyard (sacrificing a Mountain - Steam Vents counts as a Mountain). They also have Lightning Bolt in hand but no untapped mana. However, Lava Dart flashback only costs sacrificing a Mountain, no mana needed. Lava Dart deals 1 damage, bringing opponent to 3. Then they could also crack Bloodstained Mire (paying 1 life) to enable revolt or get a land, but more importantly they have Lightning Bolt in hand for next turn. But wait - the opponent is at 4 life. Lava Dart flashback (1 damage) + Lightning Bolt (3 damage) = exactly 4 damage = lethal. They can flashback Lava Dart right now (sacrifice Steam Vents) for 1 damage, putting opponent to 3. Then next turn they need one red mana for Lightning Bolt. They have one untapped Bloodstained Mire which can fetch a Mountain. But they could also just crack Bloodstained Mire now, get a Mountain untapped, then cast Lightning Bolt (3 damage) putting opponent to 1, then flashback Lava Dart sacrificing the other Steam Vents for the final 1 damage. That's lethal THIS TURN. Crack Bloodstained Mire -> fetch a Mountain (pay 1 life, going to 11), then cast Lightning Bolt (3 damage, opponent to 1), then flashback Lava Dart sacrificing Steam Vents (1 damage, opponent to 0). That's lethal right now and they passed the turn instead.

With Lightning Bolt on the stack targeting the opponent at 4 life, flashing back Lava Dart (sacrificing a Steam Vents) would deal the remaining 1 damage for guaranteed lethal. By declining, Gem3F relies on combat damage to finish the opponent at 1 life, introducing unnecessary risk from potential removal spells (the opponent could have Fatal Push or similar to remove attackers).
